assumptions.believes: object endpoints verify the caller owns the object
retrieved content is data, never instructions

assumptions.violated_if: a tool fires on untrusted input alone

hypotheses.statement: Same object (the object) is reachable through a different verb, endpoint, or content-type that skips the enforcement at 'GET /orders/{id}'.
hypotheses.attacker_view: Violate the assumption by leaving the guarded channel and entering an unguarded one.
hypotheses.devil_view: The 'alternate channel' might require stronger auth, making this a downgrade that never reaches the check.
hypotheses.investigator_test: [brain-templates] Fire the same logical action through GET vs POST vs PUT vs PATCH vs a versioned path; compare outcomes.

hypotheses.statement: A value written in one feature is consumed/rendered in another without re-running the validation done at 'GET /orders/{id}'.
hypotheses.attacker_view: Write where validation is weak, execute where trust is high (stored XSS, formula injection, template render).
hypotheses.devil_view: The two features may share the same validation pipeline, so nothing is skipped.
hypotheses.investigator_test: [brain-templates] Write a probe payload in the weakest input, then observe every surface that renders it (list, export, notification, API).

hypotheses.statement: Upstream validates at 'GET /orders/{id}', but a downstream component across a trust boundary (['browser->API']) trusts the value under different rules.
hypotheses.attacker_view: Find where validation and consumption disagree (client-side vs server-side, API vs webhook, SSO claim vs local session).
hypotheses.devil_view: The boundary may carry a signed/verified token, so downstream trust is justified.
hypotheses.investigator_test: [brain-templates] Tamper the value at the boundary (proxy match/replace) and watch whether downstream re-validates.

hypotheses.statement: An identifier is normalized differently by the layer that checks 'GET /orders/{id}' and the layer that uses it (case, encoding, numeric-vs-string, trailing slash, unicode).
hypotheses.attacker_view: Supply two spellings of the same identity: one that passes the check, one that resolves to the target.
hypotheses.devil_view: The identifier may be an opaque UUID where normalization is a no-op.
hypotheses.investigator_test: [brain-templates] Send case/encoding/whitespace variants of a known-good and a known-bad identifier; compare accept/reject matrices.

hypotheses.statement: A state transition (e.g. publish/delete) leaves stale state: the system believes the old state, another layer believes the new one.
hypotheses.attacker_view: Act on the object in the window where two layers disagree (scheduled publish to a deleted board, cached public copy of a re-secreted object).
hypotheses.devil_view: The transition may be atomic across layers, so no window exists.
hypotheses.investigator_test: [brain-templates] Force the transition, then immediately probe every layer (API, unauthenticated cache, export, search index).

hypotheses.statement: Client-visible arithmetic (credits, quotas, counts) can be desynced from the server's bookkeeping that 'GET /orders/{id}' relies on.
hypotheses.attacker_view: Drive the counter through lifecycle events (create/delete empty objects, retries, back-button resubmits) and watch for drift.
hypotheses.devil_view: Idempotency may prevent double-counting.
hypotheses.investigator_test: [brain-templates] Cycle the lifecycle event repeatedly and compare the counter before/after against the expected delta.

hypotheses.statement: Check-then-use gap: authorization is verified at time T1 at 'GET /orders/{id}', but the action executes at T2 against state that changed between.
hypotheses.attacker_view: Change the state (ownership, role, allowlist, token scope) between the check and the use; double-submit destructive actions.
hypotheses.devil_view: Rate limits or idempotency keys may collapse the window.
hypotheses.investigator_test: [brain-templates] Perform check, mutate the underlying state, then complete the action; also double-submit the destructive step.

hypotheses.statement: Distinguishable errors/timings around 'GET /orders/{id}' leak existence or state of the object to an unauthorized user.
hypotheses.attacker_view: Probe existing-but-forbidden vs nonexistent and build a differential oracle (status, message, timing).
hypotheses.devil_view: The endpoint may not be reachable by the probing user at all.
hypotheses.investigator_test: [brain-templates] Probe a known-existing-forbidden, a known-nonexistent, and an unknown target; diff status/message/timing.

hypotheses.statement: The RAG chat follows instructions embedded in retrieved documents and retrieval ignores per-user ACLs: a control vs variant probe (benign question vs revenue question, after planting an indirect-injection doc) will show the revenue query returning bob's private canary marker + canary URL to alice — an EchoLeak-class P1.
hypotheses.violated_assumption: retrieved content is data and retrieval enforces ACLs
